headline: North-West revenue drop traces to warehouse delays costing enterprise accounts.
body: Fulfilment SLA failures at WH-07 caused three of five deliveries to miss target for key enterprise accounts, prompting one to pause orders and another to threaten non-renewal [E1]. This directly shows up as enterprise active-account losses, which carry outsized revenue weight [E5]. Complaint rates rose in parallel, with SMB customers citing a competitor's faster delivery as an alternative [E3]. Marketing conversion also softened but has no supporting evidence tying it to this event, so treat it as a secondary, uncorroborated factor.

actions.action: Add 3PL overflow capacity to clear WH-07 backlog
actions.expected_impact: Restore SLA and reduce further account attrition
actions.monitoring: Daily SLA % and WH-07 backlog count

actions.action: Offer SLA guarantees to at-risk enterprise accounts
Adjust delivery-promise messaging to match real capacity

what_could_change: Confirmation that marketing conversion decline is unrelated, or new SLA data showing WH-07 recovery, would refine this view.
caveats: Marketing conversion driver lacks direct evidence and may be coincidental rather than causal.
